sections.title: Components of velocity
sections.goal: Split a launch velocity into horizontal and vertical parts.

blocks.body:
A projectile launched with speed $v_0$ at angle $\theta$ above the horizontal moves in two independent directions at once.

The horizontal and vertical components of the launch velocity are

$$
v_x = v_0 \cos\theta, \qquad v_y = v_0 \sin\theta.
$$

Ignoring air resistance, nothing pushes the projectile sideways, so $v_x$ stays the same for the whole flight. Gravity acts only on the vertical motion.

A projectile is launched at $20\ \text{m/s}$ at $60^\circ$ above the horizontal. What is $v_x$?

sections.title: Motion under gravity
sections.goal: Describe height over time and find when and where a projectile lands.

blocks.body:
With the launch point at the origin, the position after time $t$ is

$$
x(t) = v_x t, \qquad y(t) = v_y t - \tfrac{1}{2} g t^2.
$$

On level ground the projectile lands when $y(t) = 0$ again, which gives the time of flight

$$
T = \frac{2 v_0 \sin\theta}{g}.
$$

The highest point is reached halfway through, when the vertical velocity is zero.

blocks.prompt: A ball is kicked from level ground at $18\ \text{m/s}$ at $40^\circ$ above the horizontal. Take $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$ and ignore air resistance.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: How long is the ball in the air?
hints: The ball lands when its height returns to zero.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: How far does it travel horizontally before landing?
hints: Horizontal velocity is constant for the whole flight.
Multiply $v_x$ by the time of flight from part (a).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Write the maximum height in terms of `v0`, `theta`, and `g`.
hints: At the top, the vertical velocity is zero.
Use $v_y^2 = v_{y0}^2 - 2 g h$ and solve for $h$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Without calculating, explain why a launch at $50^\circ$ with the same speed lands at the same distance.

answer.rubric: A full answer says the range is $v_0^2 \sin 2\theta / g$, and that $\sin 80^\circ = \sin 100^\circ$, so complementary angles give equal ranges.

hints: Write the range in terms of $\sin 2\theta$.
